title: The Converse
short: If a² + b² = c², the triangle has a right angle.

blocks.html: The Pythagorean theorem says right triangles satisfy $a^{2} + b^{2} = c^{2}$. The converse runs the other way: a triangle whose sides satisfy it must have a right angle. Builders use this to check square corners.

Suppose a triangle has sides $a$, $b$, $c$ with $a^{2} + b^{2} = c^{2}$. Build a right triangle with legs $a$ and $b$. By the theorem, its hypotenuse is $\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}} = c$. So the two triangles have the same three side lengths. Three sticks can be joined into a triangle in only one shape, so the triangles are congruent, and the first triangle has the same right angle.
Converse: if the sides of a triangle satisfy $a^{2} + b^{2} = c^{2}$, where $c$ is the longest side, then the triangle has a right angle, opposite $c$. If they don’t, it has no right angle.

blocks.name: pythagoras
blocks.cap: Change the angle between $a$ and $b$. The squares on the legs match the square on the third side only at exactly $90^\circ$.

blocks.title: A square corner
blocks.q: A builder measures 3 ft along one wall and 4 ft along the other, and the diagonal between those marks is 5 ft. Is the corner square?
steps: By the converse, the corner is a right angle.

blocks.html: If $c^{2}$ is greater than $a^{2} + b^{2}$, the angle across from $c$ is wider than $90^\circ$ (as with 6, 8, 11). If it is less, the angle is narrower.
Testing with a side that isn’t the longest as $c$. For 15, 8, 17, the test is $8^{2} + 15^{2} = 17^{2}$ (true), not $8^{2} + 17^{2} = 15^{2}$. Always put the longest side alone on one side.
